        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * OnboardingContainerView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct OnboardingContainerView: View {\n    // Access the horizontal size class from the environment to distinguish between compact (iPhone) and regular (iPad) layouts\n    @Environment(\\.horizontalSizeClass) var horizontalSizeClass\n    // Binding to control whether the onboarding is presented\n    @Binding var isPresented: Bool\n    // Tracks the current page in the onboarding flow\n    @State private var currentPage = 0\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        #if os(macOS)\n        // Use the macOS-specific onboarding container view\n        MacOnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n        #else\n        if horizontalSizeClass == .compact {\n            // Show the iPhone-specific onboarding container view for compact width devices\n            iPhone_OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n        } else {\n            // Show the iPad-specific onboarding container view for regular width devices\n            iPad_OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n        }\n        #endif\n    }\n}\n\n// Preview provider for SwiftUI previews\nstruct OnboardingContainerView_Previews: PreviewProvider {\n    @State static var isPresented = true\n    static var previews: some View {\n        OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented)\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./APP_FEATURES.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 28

        },
        "contents": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\n\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\n\n## App Navigation and Views\n**For users:**\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\n\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\n\n## Location Tracking\n**For users:**\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\n\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

            "text": "- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./APP_FEATURES.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 132
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 161
          }
        },
        "contents": "**For developers:**\n- &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &#96;Application Support&#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly. A &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; caches routes by device and transport, with distance‑based invalidation.\n- Static map elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96; are rasterized and cached with keys that include color scheme and display scale; renderers respect Dynamic Type and set &#96;isOpaque=false&#96; where appropriate.\n\n## Haptic Feedback and UI Enhancements\n**For users:**\n- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle haptic feedback, pulsing accuracy circles show location precision, and shimmering indicators highlight loading states.\n\n- Animations for pulsing/shimmer are automatically reduced in Low Power Mode or when the app is backgrounded to save energy.\n\n**For developers:**\n- The &#96;Haptic&#96; utility abstracts platform differences. Shared UI elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;, &#96;MapCompass&#96;, and &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; reside under &#96;views/Common&#96; and are reused across device and group map views.\n\n## Multi‑platform Support\n**For users:**\n- The interface adapts to iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with platform‑specific root views and onboarding flows. iPhone uses a tab bar, iPad presents split views, and Mac currently mirrors the iPhone experience in a resizable window.\n\n- On iPad, you can open device details in separate windows for multitasking.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects the appropriate root view using size classes and platform checks. Dedicated onboarding containers exist for each platform, and many components in &#96;views/Common&#96; are platform agnostic.\n\n## Localization and Accessibility\n**For users:**\n- Available in English, German, and Japanese, with dynamic type and accessibility labels and hints applied to buttons, tab items, and swipe actions.\n\n- VoiceOver support has been improved across lists and map controls. Alerts and route‑limit messages are localized.",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * Mac_OnboardingContainerView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct Mac_OnboardingContainerView: View {\n    @Binding var isPresented: Bool\n    @Binding var currentPage: Int\n    \n    private let pages: [AnyView] = [\n        AnyView(iPhone_1_OnboardingWelcomeView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_2_OnboardingLocationPermissionView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_3_OnboardingServerView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_4_OnboardingLocationHistoryView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_5_OnboardingQRcodeView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_6_OnboardingDoneView())\n    ]\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        VStack {\n            TabView(selection: $currentPage) {\n                ForEach(0..&lt;pages.count, id: \\.self) { index in\n                    pages[index]\n                        .tag(index)\n                }\n            }\n            .tabViewStyle(PageTabViewStyle())\n            .indexViewStyle(PageIndexViewStyle(backgroundDisplayMode: .always))\n            \n            HStack {\n                if currentPage &gt; 0 {\n                    Button(\"Previous\") { currentPage -= 1 }\n                }\n                Spacer()\n                if currentPage &lt; pages.count - 1 {\n                    Button(\"Next\") { currentPage += 1 }\n                } else {\n                    Button(\"Finish\") {\n                        UserDefaults.standard.hasCompletedOnboarding = true\n                        isPresented = false\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            .padding()\n        }\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground))\n        .ignoresSafeArea()\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground).ignoresSafeArea())\n    }\n}\n\nstruct Mac_OnboardingContainerView_Previews: PreviewProvider {\n    @State static var isPresented = true\n    @State static var currentPage = 0",

        "contents": "# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\n\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\n\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\n\n### Technology Stack\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\n\n### Core Components\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\n├── LocationManagers/\n│   └── LocationManager.swift\n├── SettingsManagers/\n│   └── App Settings/ (SettingsManager, thisDeviceIDManager, Settings.bundle)\n│   └── Devices/ (KnownDevice, KnownDeviceStore)\n│   └── Groups/ (DeviceGroup, DeviceGroupStore)\n├── views/\n│   ├── Common/ (Shared UI)\n│   ├── iPhone/ (iPhone-specific)\n│   ├── iPad/ (iPad-specific)\n│   └── Mac/ (onboarding previews only)\n└── Assets/ (Resources &amp; Localization)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Common Components Overview\n\n- Shared UI (&#96;views/Common/&#96;):\n  - &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96;, &#96;ViewModifiers&#96; (adaptive toolbars/navigation)\n  - Device &amp; group UI: &#96;DeviceRowView&#96;, &#96;GroupRowView&#96;, &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96;, &#96;DeviceBatterySymbol&#96;\n  - Map UI &amp; helpers (&#96;views/Common/Map/&#96;): &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; (+ &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96;), &#96;MapCompass&#96;, &#96;OffScreenDeviceArrow&#96;, &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96;, &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96;, &#96;RouteStyle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;\n- Data &amp; Caching:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving under Application Support)",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * PlaybackSpeedOverlay.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2026-01-05.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\n/// A centered overlay that briefly displays the current playback speed.\nstruct PlaybackSpeedOverlay: View {\n    let speed: Double\n\n    var body: some View {\n        VStack(spacing: 8) {\n            Image(systemName: speed &gt; 1.0 ? \"forward.fill\" : \"play.fill\")\n                .font(.system(size: 28, weight: .semibold))\n                .foregroundStyle(.primary)\n\n            Text(String(format: NSLocalizedString(\"playback_speed_format\", comment: \"Playback speed indicator format like 1x or 2x\"), speed))\n                .font(.system(size: 24, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))\n                .foregroundStyle(.primary)\n        }\n        .padding(.horizontal, 32)\n        .padding(.vertical, 24)\n        .background {\n            if #available(iOS 26.0, *) {\n                Color.clear\n                    .glassEffect(in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))\n            } else {\n                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)\n                    .fill(.ultraThinMaterial)\n                    .overlay(\n                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)\n                            .fill(Color.black.opacity(0.4))\n                    )\n            }\n        }\n        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 16, x: 0, y: 8)\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    ZStack {\n        Color.gray.opacity(0.3)\n            .ignoresSafeArea()\n\n        PlaybackSpeedOverlay(speed: 2.0)\n    }\n}",

defaultLabel : viewModel.label)\n                .font(.caption2)\n                .foregroundColor(.primary)\n                .lineLimit(1)\n                .minimumScaleFactor(0.5)\n            Rectangle()\n                .frame(width: width, height: 2)\n                .foregroundColor(.primary)\n                .cornerRadius(4)\n        }\n        .frame(width: width)\n        .padding(4)\n        .background(.ultraThinMaterial)\n        .cornerRadius(8)\n        .onAppear {\n            viewModel.schedule(region: region, width: width)\n        }\n        .onChange(of: regionToken) { _, _ in\n            viewModel.schedule(region: region, width: width)\n        }\n        .onChange(of: width) { _, newValue in\n            viewModel.schedule(region: region, width: newValue)\n        }\n        .onChange(of: colorScheme) { _, _ in\n            // Force recalculation to ensure colors and label adapt on theme changes\n            viewModel.schedule(region: region, width: width)\n        }\n    }\n\n    private var defaultLabel: String {\n        // Localized: Placeholder text while computing scale\n        NSLocalizedString(\"scalebar_computing\", comment: \"Scale bar: computing distance placeholder\")\n    }\n\n    private struct RegionToken: Equatable {\n        let latBucket: Int\n        let lonBucket: Int\n        let latDeltaBucket: Int\n        let lonDeltaBucket: Int\n    }\n\n    private var regionToken: RegionToken {\n        let latBucket = Int((region.center.latitude * 1000.0).rounded())",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * ColorExtensions.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2025-01-25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\n// MARK: - Color Extension for Contrast Adjustment\nextension Color {\n    /// Adjusts device color for better contrast in light/dark mode\n    /// - Parameters:\n    ///   - deviceColor: The original device color\n    ///   - colorScheme: Current color scheme (light/dark)\n    /// - Returns: Adjusted color with better contrast\n    static func adjustedDeviceColor(_ deviceColor: Color, for colorScheme: ColorScheme) -&gt; Color {\n        // Convert to UIColor for easier manipulation\n        let uiColor = UIColor(deviceColor)\n        \n        // Get RGB components\n        var red: CGFloat = 0\n        var green: CGFloat = 0\n        var blue: CGFloat = 0\n        var alpha: CGFloat = 0\n        \n        uiColor.getRed(&amp;red, green: &amp;green, blue: &amp;blue, alpha: &amp;alpha)\n        \n        // Calculate luminance to determine if color is dark or light\n        let luminance = 0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue\n        \n        switch colorScheme {\n        case .light:\n            // In light mode, if the color is too light (white-ish), make it lighter gray\n            if luminance &gt; 0.85 {\n                // Make it a light gray instead of white\n                return Color(red: 0.8, green: 0.8, blue: 0.8)\n            }\n        case .dark:\n            // In dark mode, if the color is too dark (black-ish), make it darker gray\n            if luminance &lt; 0.15 {\n                // Make it a dark gray instead of black\n                return Color(red: 0.3, green: 0.3, blue: 0.3)\n            }\n        @unknown default:\n            break\n        }\n        \n        // Return original color if no adjustment needed\n        return deviceColor\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "///   device point.\n\nstruct OffScreenDeviceArrow: View {\n    let deviceName: String\n    let deviceColor: Color\n    let screenCenter: CGPoint\n    let deviceCoordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D\n    let mapRegion: MKCoordinateRegion\n    let screenSize: CGSize\n    /// Distance between the map center and the device in kilometers.         "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * ErrorOverlay.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\nimport Combine\n\nstruct ErrorOverlay: View {\n    let message: String\n    let visible: Bool\n\n    var body: some View {\n        if visible {\n            VStack {\n                Spacer()\n                HStack {\n                    Spacer()\n                    Text(message)\n                        .padding(16)\n                        .background(Color.red.opacity(0.85))\n                        .foregroundColor(.white)\n                        .cornerRadius(12)\n                        .shadow(radius: 10)\n                        .multilineTextAlignment(.center)\n                    Spacer()\n                }\n                Spacer()\n            }\n            .transition(.scale.combined(with: .opacity))\n            .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: visible)\n            .zIndex(1)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nclass ErrorOverlayManager: ObservableObject {\n    @Published var message: String = \"\"\n    @Published var visible: Bool = false\n\n    private var hideCancellable: AnyCancellable?\n\n    func show(message: String, duration: TimeInterval = 3.0) {\n        self.message = message\n        withAnimation {\n            self.visible = true\n        }\n        hideCancellable?.cancel()\n        hideCancellable = Just(())\n            .delay(for: .seconds(duration), scheduler: DispatchQueue.main)\n            .sink { [weak self] _ in\n                withAnimation {\n                    self?.visible = false\n                }\n            }\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    ErrorOverlay(message: \"This is an example error message!\", visible: true)\n        .background(Color.gray.opacity(0.2))\n        .edgesIgnoringSafeArea(.all)\n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * MiataruMapMarker.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n#if canImport(UIKit)\nimport UIKit\n#elseif canImport(AppKit)\nimport AppKit\n#endif\n\n// Hilfs-Extension für Kontrastbestimmung\nextension Color {\n    /// Returns true if the color is considered 'light' (für Kontrast)\n    func isLight(threshold: Float = 0.6) -&gt; Bool {\n#if canImport(UIKit)\n        let uiColor = UIColor(self)\n        var r: CGFloat = 0, g: CGFloat = 0, b: CGFloat = 0, a: CGFloat = 0\n        uiColor.getRed(&amp;r, green: &amp;g, blue: &amp;b, alpha: &amp;a)\n        let luminance = 0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b\n        return Float(luminance) &gt; threshold\n#else\n        return false // macOS: ggf. NSColor analog\n#endif\n    }\n}\n\n// Zusatz-Utilities für Cache-Key und Bild-Cache\nextension Color {\n    /// Stabile RGBA-Repräsentation für Cache-Keys\n    func rgbaKey() -&gt; String {\n#if canImport(UIKit)\n        let uiColor = UIColor(self)\n        var r: CGFloat = 0, g: CGFloat = 0, b: CGFloat = 0, a: CGFloat = 0\n        uiColor.getRed(&amp;r, green: &amp;g, blue: &amp;b, alpha: &amp;a)\n        return String(format: \"r%.3fg%.3fb%.3fa%.3f\", r, g, b, a)\n#elseif canImport(AppKit)\n        return String(describing: self)\n#else\n        return String(describing: self)\n#endif\n    }\n}\n\nfinal class MiataruMapMarkerImageCache {\n    static let shared = MiataruMapMarkerImageCache()\n    private let cache = NSCache&lt;NSString, PlatformImage&gt;()\n    private init() {\n        cache.countLimit = 256\n    }\n    func image(for key: String) -&gt; PlatformImage? {\n        cache.object(forKey: key as NSString)\n    }\n    func set(_ image: PlatformImage, for key: String, cost: Int = 0) {\n        cache.setObject(image, forKey: key as NSString, cost: cost)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct MiataruMapMarker: View {\n    @Environment(\\.colorScheme) private var colorScheme",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * PulsingAccuracyCircle.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\n/// A reusable, GPU-friendly indicator for visualizing location accuracy and\n/// presence. Designed for Miataru to be placed under the user's pin or any\n/// tracked device, it renders a stable core with outward-expanding halos to\n/// communicate activity/accuracy without the core size visually collapsing.\n///\n\n/// Implementation overview:\n/// - The view consists of a constant-size core circle and two halos.\n/// - Each halo scales from 1.0 to &#96;haloMaxScale&#96; with staggered delays to create\n///   a layered rhythm. The animation repeats forever with an ease-out curve.\n/// - The container frame is set to &#96;size * haloMaxScale&#96; to account for the\n///   largest halo extent and prevent clipping.\n/// - Rendering is flattened with &#96;drawingGroup()&#96; to reduce 3D perspective\n///   warping when composited in MapKit overlays/annotations.\n///\n/// Typical use cases:\n/// - Under the user's current location marker to visualize GPS accuracy.\n/// - Behind tracked devices to indicate presence or recent updates.\n/// - As a subtle attention cue in lists or detail views.\n///\n/// Customization:\n/// - Use the initializer to tweak scale, opacities, and animation timings.\n/// - &#96;size&#96; controls the core diameter; halos expand proportionally.\n/// - &#96;pulsingColor&#96; accepts any SwiftUI &#96;Color&#96; (gradients are derived from it).\n///\n/// Accessibility:\n/// - This view is purely decorative. Consider marking it hidden from\n///   accessibility where embedded (e.g., &#96;.accessibilityHidden(true)&#96;) and\n///   provide descriptive labels on the parent control/annotation as needed.\n///\n/// Example:\n/// &#96;&#96;&#96;swift\n/// PulsingAccuracyCircle(\n///     pulsingColor: .orange,\n///     size: 172,\n///     haloMaxScale: 1.8\n/// )\n/// &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nstruct PulsingAccuracyCircle: View {\n\n    @State private var isPulsing = false",

some View {\n        content\n            .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: Notification.Name.NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange)) { _ in\n                isLowPowerMode = ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled\n            }\n            .environment(\\.shimmeringAllowed, active &amp;&amp;         "contents": "    }\n\n    private func formattedDate(_ timestamp: Double) -&gt; String {\n        let date = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: timestamp)\n        return iPhone_DeviceHistoryMapView.timelineDayFormatter.string(from: date)\n    }\n\n    private func rangeHandle(x: CGFloat, systemName: String) -&gt; some View {\n        let visualHandleSize: CGFloat = 26\n        let hitTargetSize: CGFloat = 44 // Increase touch target for easier dragging\n\n        return Capsule()\n            .fill(.thinMaterial)\n            .frame(width: visualHandleSize, height: visualHandleSize)\n            .overlay(\n                Image(systemName: systemName)\n                    .font(.system(size: 10, weight: .bold))\n                    .foregroundStyle(Color.primary)\n            )\n            .shadow(radius: 2)\n            .frame(width: hitTargetSize, height: hitTargetSize)\n            .contentShape(Rectangle())\n            .offset(x: x - (hitTargetSize / 2))\n            .frame(maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .center)\n    }\n\n    private func clamp(_ value: Double, to range: ClosedRange&lt;Double&gt;) -&gt; Double {\n        min(max(value, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound)\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "# CodeScanner\n\n&lt;p&gt;\n    &lt;img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-13.0+-blue.svg\" /&gt;\n    &lt;img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-5.1-ff69b4.svg\" /&gt;\n    &lt;a href=\"https://twitter.com/twostraws\"&gt;\n        &lt;img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/Contact-@twostraws-lightgrey.svg?style=flat\" alt=\"Twitter: @twostraws\" /&gt;\n    &lt;/a&gt;\n&lt;/p&gt;\n\nCodeScanner is a SwiftUI framework that makes it easy to scan codes such as QR codes and barcodes. It provides a view struct, &#96;CodeScannerView&#96;, that can be shown inside a sheet so that all scanning occurs in one place.\n\n\n## Basic usage\n\nYou should create an instance of &#96;CodeScannerView&#96; with at least two parameters: an array of the types to scan for, and a closure that will be called when a result is ready.\n\nYour completion closure must accept a &#96;Result&lt;ScanResult, ScanError&gt;&#96;, where the success case is the code string and type that was found. For example, if you asked to scan for QR codes and bar codes, you might be told that a QR code containing the email address paul@hackingwithswift.com was found.\n\nIf things go wrong, your result will contain a &#96;ScanError&#96; set to one of these three cases:\n\n- &#96;badInput&#96;, if the camera cannot be accessed\n- &#96;badOutput&#96;, if the camera is not capable of detecting codes\n- &#96;initError&#96;, if initialization failed.\n\n**Important:** iOS *requires* you to add the \"Privacy - Camera Usage Description\" key to your Info.plist file, providing a reason for why you want to access the camera.\n\n\n## Customization options\n\nYou can provide a variety of extra customization options to &#96;CodeScannerView&#96; in its initializer:\n\n- &#96;scanMode&#96; can be &#96;.once&#96; to scan a single code, &#96;.oncePerCode&#96; to scan many codes but only trigger finding each unique code once, and &#96;.continuous&#96; will keep finding codes until you dismiss the scanner. Default: &#96;.once&#96;.\n- &#96;scanInterval&#96; controls how fast individual codes should be scanned (in seconds) when running in &#96;.continuous&#96; scan mode.\n- &#96;showViewfinder&#96; determines whether to show a box-like viewfinder over the UI. Default: false.\n- &#96;simulatedData&#96; allows you to provide some test data to use in Simulator, when real scanning isn’t available. Default: an empty string.",

AVMetadataMachineReadableCodeObject,\n              let stringValue = readableObject.stringValue else {\n\n            return\n        }\n\n        handler = { [weak self] image in\n            guard let self else { return }\n            let result = ScanResult(string: stringValue, type: readableObject.type, image: image, corners: readableObject.corners)\n\n            switch parentView.scanMode {\n            case .once:\n                found(result)\n                // make sure we only trigger scan once per use\n                didFinishScanning = true\n\n            case .manual:\n                if !didFinishScanning, isWithinManualCaptureInterval {\n                    found(result)\n                    didFinishScanning = true\n                }\n\n            case .oncePerCode:\n                if !codesFound.contains(stringValue) {\n                    codesFound.insert(stringValue)\n                    found(result)\n                }\n\n            case .continuous:\n                if isPastScanInterval {\n                    found(result)\n                }\n\n            case .continuousExcept(let ignoredList):\n                if isPastScanInterval, !ignoredList.contains(stringValue) {\n                    found(result)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if parentView.requiresPhotoOutput {\n            isCapturing = true\n            photoOutput.capturePhoto(with: AVCapturePhotoSettings(), delegate: self)\n        } else {\n            handler?(nil)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// MARK: - UIImagePickerControllerDelegate\n\n@available(macCatalyst 14.0, *)\nextension CodeScannerView.ScannerViewController: UIImagePickerControllerDelegate {\n    ",

        "contents": "// MARK: - UIImagePickerControllerDelegate\n\n@available(macCatalyst 14.0, *)\nextension CodeScannerView.ScannerViewController: UIImagePickerControllerDelegate {\n    public func imagePickerController(_ picker: UIImagePickerController, didFinishPickingMediaWithInfo info: [UIImagePickerController.InfoKey: Any]) {\n        isGalleryShowing = false\n\n        defer {\n            dismiss(animated: true)\n        }\n\n        guard let qrcodeImg = info[.originalImage] as? UIImage,\n              let detector = CIDetector(ofType: CIDetectorTypeQRCode, context: nil, options: [CIDetectorAccuracy: CIDetectorAccuracyHigh]),\n              let ciImage = CIImage(image:qrcodeImg) else {\n\n            return\n        }\n\n        let features = detector.features(in: ciImage)\n\n        guard !features.isEmpty else {\n            didFail(reason: .badOutput)\n            return\n        } \n        for feature in features.compactMap({ $0 as? CIQRCodeFeature }) {\n            guard let qrCodeLink = feature.messageString, !qrCodeLink.isEmpty else {\n                didFail(reason: .badOutput)\n                continue\n            }\n\n            let corners = [\n                feature.bottomLeft,\n                feature.bottomRight,\n                feature.topRight,\n                feature.topLeft\n            ]\n\n            let result = ScanResult(string: qrCodeLink, type: .qr, image: qrcodeImg, corners: corners)\n            found(result)\n        }\n    }\n\n    public func imagePickerControllerDidCancel(_ picker: UIImagePickerController) {\n        isGalleryShowing = false\n        dismiss(animated: true)\n    }\n}\n\n// MARK: - UIAdaptivePresentationControllerDelegate\n\n@available(macCatalyst 14.0, *)\nextension CodeScannerView.ScannerViewController: UIAdaptivePresentationControllerDelegate {\n    public func presentationControllerDidDismiss(_ presentationController: UIPresentationController) {\n        // Gallery is no longer being presented\n        isGalleryShowing = false\n    }\n}\n\n// MARK: - AVCapturePhotoCaptureDelegate\n\n@available(macCatalyst 14.0, *)\nextension CodeScannerView.ScannerViewController: AVCapturePhotoCaptureDelegate {\n    \n    public func photoOutput(\n        _ output: AVCapturePhotoOutput,",

This will be sent the string that was detected or a &#96;ScanError&#96;.\n/// For testing inside the simulator, set the &#96;simulatedData&#96; property to some test data you want to send back.\n@available(macCatalyst 14.0, *)\npublic struct CodeScannerView: UIViewControllerRepresentable {\n    \n    public let codeTypes: [AVMetadataObject.ObjectType]\n    public let scanMode: ScanMode\n    public let manualSelect: Bool\n    public let scanInterval: Double\n    public let showViewfinder: Bool\n    public let requiresPhotoOutput: Bool\n    public var simulatedData = \"\"\n    public var shouldVibrateOnSuccess: Bool\n    public var isTorchOn: Bool\n    public var isPaused: Bool\n    public var isGalleryPresented: Binding&lt;Bool&gt;\n    public var videoCaptureDevice: AVCaptureDevice?\n    public var completion: (Result&lt;ScanResult, ScanError&gt;) -&gt; Void\n\n    public init(\n        codeTypes: [AVMetadataObject.ObjectType],\n        scanMode: ScanMode = .once,\n        manualSelect: Bool = false,\n        scanInterval: Double = 2.0,\n        showViewfinder: Bool = false,\n        requiresPhotoOutput: Bool = true,\n        simulatedData: String = \"\",\n        shouldVibrateOnSuccess: Bool = true,\n        isTorchOn: Bool = false,\n        isPaused: Bool = false,\n        isGalleryPresented: Binding&lt;Bool&gt; = .constant(false),\n        videoCaptureDevice: AVCaptureDevice? = AVCaptureDevice.bestForVideo,\n        completion: @escaping (Result&lt;ScanResult, ScanError&gt;) -&gt; Void\n    ) {\n        self.codeTypes = codeTypes\n        self.scanMode = scanMode",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nstruct QRCodeScannerExampleView: View {\n    @State private var isPresentingScanner = false\n    @State private var scannedCode: String?\n\n    var body: some View {\n        VStack(spacing: 10) {\n            if let code = scannedCode {\n                NavigationLink(\"Next page\", destination: NextView(scannedCode: code), isActive: .constant(true)).hidden()\n            }\n\n            Button(\"Scan Code\") {\n                isPresentingScanner = true\n            }\n\n            Text(\"Scan a QR code to begin\")\n        }\n        .sheet(isPresented: $isPresentingScanner) {\n            CodeScannerView(codeTypes: [.qr]) { response in\n                if case let .success(result) = response {\n                    scannedCode = result.string\n                    isPresentingScanner = false\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Scanning small QR codes\n\nScanning small QR code on devices with dual or tripple cameras has to be adjusted because of minimum focus distance built in these cameras.\nTo have the best possible focus on the code we scan it is needed to choose the most suitable camera and apply recommended zoom factor.\n\nExample for scanning 20x20mm QR codes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nCodeScannerView(codeTypes: [.qr], videoCaptureDevice: AVCaptureDevice.zoomedCameraForQRCode(withMinimumCodeSize: 20)) { response in                    \n    switch response {\n    case .success(let result):\n        print(\"Found code: \\(result.string)\")\n    case .failure(let error):\n        print(error.localizedDescription)\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n## Credits\n\nCodeScanner was made by [Paul Hudson](https://twitter.com/twostraws), who writes [free Swift tutorials over at Hacking with Swift](https://www.hackingwithswift.com), and is now maintained by [Nathan Fallet](https://nathanfallet.me). All rights reserved.\n//\n\n#if os(iOS)\nimport AVFoundation\nimport SwiftUI\n\n/// An enum describing the ways CodeScannerView can hit scanning problems.\npublic enum ScanError: Error {\n    /// The camera could not be accessed.\n    case badInput\n\n    /// The camera was not capable of scanning the requested codes.\n    case badOutput\n\n    /// Initialization failed.\n    case initError(_ error: Error)\n  \n    /// The camera permission is denied \n    case permissionDenied\n}\n\n/// The result from a successful scan: the string that was scanned, and also the type of data that was found.\n/// The type is useful for times when you've asked to scan several different code types at the same time, because\n/// it will report the exact code type that was found.\n@available(macCatalyst 14.0, *)\npublic struct ScanResult {\n    /// The contents of the code.\n    public let string: String\n\n    /// The type of code that was matched.\n    public let type: AVMetadataObject.ObjectType\n    \n    /// The image of the code that was matched\n    public let image: UIImage?\n  \n    /// The corner coordinates of the scanned code.\n    public let corners: [CGPoint]\n}\n\n/// The operating mode for CodeScannerView.\npublic enum ScanMode {\n    /// Scan exactly one code, then stop.\n    case once\n\n    /// Scan each code no more than once.\n    case oncePerCode\n\n    /// Keep scanning all codes until dismissed.\n    case continuous\n\n    /// Keep scanning all codes - except the ones from the ignored list - until dismissed.\n    case continuousExcept(ignoredList: Set&lt;String&gt;)\n\n    /// Scan only when capture button is tapped.\n    case manual\n\n    var isManual: Bool {\n        switch self {\n        case .manual:\n            return true\n        case .once, .oncePerCode, .continuous, .continuousExcept:\n            return false\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A SwiftUI view that is able to scan barcodes, QR codes, and more, and send back what was found.\n/// To use, set &#96;codeTypes&#96; to be an array of things to scan for, e.g. &#96;[.qr]&#96;, and set &#96;completion&#96; to",

        "contents": "extension CodeScannerView.ScannerViewController: AVCapturePhotoCaptureDelegate {\n    \n    public func photoOutput(\n        _ output: AVCapturePhotoOutput,\n        didFinishProcessingPhoto photo: AVCapturePhoto,\n        error: Error?\n    ) {\n        isCapturing = false\n        guard let imageData = photo.fileDataRepresentation() else {\n            print(\"Error while generating image from photo capture data.\");\n            return\n        }\n        guard let qrImage = UIImage(data: imageData) else {\n            print(\"Unable to generate UIImage from image data.\");\n            return\n        }\n        handler?(qrImage)\n    }\n    \n    public func photoOutput(\n        _ output: AVCapturePhotoOutput,\n        willCapturePhotoFor resolvedSettings: AVCaptureResolvedPhotoSettings\n    ) {\n        AudioServicesDisposeSystemSoundID(1108)\n    }\n    \n    public func photoOutput(\n        _ output: AVCapturePhotoOutput,\n        didCapturePhotoFor resolvedSettings: AVCaptureResolvedPhotoSettings\n    ) {\n        AudioServicesDisposeSystemSoundID(1108)\n    }\n    \n}\n\n// MARK: - AVCaptureDevice\n\n@available(macCatalyst 14.0, *)\npublic extension AVCaptureDevice {\n    \n    /// This returns the Ultra Wide Camera on capable devices and the default Camera for Video otherwise.\n    static var bestForVideo: AVCaptureDevice? {\n        let deviceHasUltraWideCamera = !AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession(deviceTypes: [.builtInUltraWideCamera], mediaType: .video, position: .back).devices.isEmpty\n        return deviceHasUltraWideCamera ?         "contents": "            }\n        }\n      \n        private func addOrientationDidChangeObserver() {\n            NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(\n                self,\n                selector: #selector(updateOrientation),\n                name: UIDevice.orientationDidChangeNotification,\n                object: nil\n            )\n        }\n      \n        private func setBackgroundColor(_ color: UIColor = .black) {\n            view.backgroundColor = color\n        }\n      \n        private func setupCaptureDevice() {\n            captureSession = AVCaptureSession()\n\n            guard let videoCaptureDevice = parentView.videoCaptureDevice ?? fallbackVideoCaptureDevice else {\n                return\n            }\n\n            let videoInput: AVCaptureDeviceInput\n\n            do {\n                videoInput = try AVCaptureDeviceInput(device: videoCaptureDevice)\n            } catch {\n                didFail(reason: .initError(error))\n                return\n            }\n\n            if captureSession!.canAddInput(videoInput) {\n                captureSession!.addInput(videoInput)\n            } else {\n                didFail(reason: .badInput)\n                return\n            }\n            let metadataOutput = AVCaptureMetadataOutput()\n\n            if captureSession!.canAddOutput(metadataOutput) {\n                captureSession!.addOutput(metadataOutput)\n                captureSession!.addOutput(photoOutput)\n                metadataOutput.setMetadataObjectsDelegate(self, queue: DispatchQueue.main)\n                metadataOutput.metadataObjectTypes = parentView.codeTypes\n            } else {\n                didFail(reason: .badOutput)\n                return\n            }\n        }\n\n        private func addViewFinder() {\n            guard showViewfinder, let imageView = viewFinder else { return }",
